cloudflare.measurement_note: Rounded dashboard figures. IP-based network traffic, not verified human sessions. Overview may include bots, partial requests and subrequests.

resend.interpretation: Two request notifications, not four enquiries; not confirmed appointments or paying clients. No personal email addresses or message contents are included.

conversion_rate_note: Not calculated: dashboard periods differ and the Cloudflare overview is not a matching human-session denominator.

figures.caption: Brandit’s live public website. The homepage explains the offer and provides routes to an introductory call and client login. Public-site capture, 19 October 2026.
Dedicated Brandit assessment workspace. The same named operator, Michal Kowalczyk, is used throughout this walkthrough. The workspace opens directly into the invoicing service.
Digital-credit offer and pricing. The application presents 1, 10 and 50-token options with total and per-invoice prices. This assessment simulation leaves checkout disabled.
Alexander’s Cloudflare traffic overview. Domain: alexanderlajertherapy.com. Selected period: 19 September–19 October 2026. Values are shown as rounded by Cloudflare; the account sidebar is collapsed.
A clear audience, location and next step. The public homepage connects North London service positioning to a free introductory call.
Content tailored to a specific audience. The parent-focused page addresses visitor questions and links towards the contact journey.

Explaining the offer before asking for an enquiry. The live service details describe visibility and operational support, with an introductory-call action in the navigation. The expanded descriptions explain what prospective customers can enquire about.
Alicia’s service and location positioning. The homepage brings together relevant service wording, location and a visible contact route. Public-site capture from 18 October 2026.
A published article as a search entry point. “Holding the frame” has its own page title, description, canonical URL and BlogPosting structured data, checked on the live page.
A dedicated service page. The children’s service page has a specific search title describing the service and London locations.

Alexander’s domain-filtered Resend metrics. Selected domain: alexanderlajertherapy.com; period: 5–19 October 2026. Four emails were delivered. Checking their types identifies two call-request notifications and two acknowledgements, rather than four enquiries.
The therapist’s enquiry notification. Rendered from the project’s actual email-template function using Michal’s assessment scenario. This is a template simulation; no message was sent.
The visitor’s acknowledgement. The matching template addresses the same assessment user and confirms receipt. This second email belongs to the same enquiry, rather than creating another lead.
Preparing the invoice batch. Michal’s assessment workspace shows one Assessment Client, two dated £70 charges and a £140 total.
Reviewing cost and token use. The final check shows the invoice total and the resulting token balance before sending. Sending remains disabled in the assessment simulation.
Previewing the invoice and recipient email. The same operator, client and £140 example carry through to the documents. All addresses and bank details are designated assessment examples.
Providing a record after the transaction. A single synthetic prior invoice illustrates status visibility and PDF access. It is a demonstration record.

Brandit’s live discovery-call booking page. The public form shows the available steps, the no-payment explanation and an alternative contact route. The form is empty; no booking was submitted for this report.
Choosing an introductory-call route. The visitor selects an audience and a provisional slot. The page explains what happens next.
Collecting the details needed to respond. The second step asks for contact details and optional context. The form was not submitted; the Cloudflare success indicator refers to the browser check.
Offering an alternative to a call. Visitors can choose a message instead, reducing friction for people who prefer email. This screenshot shows an empty form.
Making fees and contact choices visible. Alicia’s contact page explains the fee range, response expectations and enquiry process. Public-site capture from 18 October 2026.
